analyst.summary: DMart remains one of India's best-run retailers - a cash-generative, historically debt-free business still expanding its physical store network at a record pace - but its growth engine is visibly downshifting. Same-store sales growth has fallen from over 7% to 5.5% over the past year, driven almost entirely by stagnation in its most profitable big-city stores as quick-commerce apps such as Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart capture a fast-growing share of urban grocery spend; DMart's own online arm, DMart Ready, is shrinking its city footprint even as its losses grow. Profit is now compounding meaningfully slower than revenue, showing up as margin compression rather than the pure scale-driven growth its rich valuation - about 84 times trailing earnings on a modest 13% return on equity - still assumes. We rate it a Sell: a well-run business priced for a growth rate it is no longer delivering.
